stories.headline: Enzo Maresca: 'It's my duty' to help Phil Foden rediscover best Man City form
stories.summary: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca feels a duty to help Phil Foden return to his best.
stories.body:
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca feels a duty to help Phil Foden return to his best.

Foden is enjoying a resurgence having scored four goals in his last two games since serving a domestic suspension.

The 26-year-old's performances, which included a hat trick against AEK Athens in midweek, have raised the prospect of a return to the England fold after being dropped for the World Cup.

Maresca has taken a keen interest in Foden's wellbeing since taking over at the Etihad Stadium in the summer.

The Italian said: "Since we started, I sat down with Phil two or three times -- especially at the beginning -- just to show him, I don't know if love is the right word to use, but to show him how important he is.

"I know Phil from years ago, so I know how good he is. For different reasons, the last few years he was not good enough but I think when you have players like Phil available you are a better team because it's a matter of improving players.

"For me, it's my duty to try to help him to be one of the best players in England again."

Maresca is also determined to help playmaker Rayan Cherki maximise his threat.

The French playmaker has showcased his dazzling ability with fine goals against Liverpool and AEK in recent weeks.

Maresca, however, feels the 23-year-old would be even more dangerous if he could improve his sense of positioning.

He said: "In this moment Rayan is one of the best players in Europe. When he is in the right position -- that means when we are able to find him between the lines -- he's always dangerous.

"Sometimes, because he loves the ball and he loves to move a lot, most of the time he is in the wrong position, but when he is in the right position he is always a weapon for us."

Maresca accepts, however, that he must strike a balance between improving Cherki's awareness and preserving the instincts that make him such a threat.

- Phil Foden: Still 'long way' from my best despite hat trick in Man City rout

- Football watchdog chair asserts 'absolute' power to force City sale

- VAR who incorrectly awarded Erling Haaland goal reinstated to Premier League

Speaking at a news conference to preview Saturday's trip to Aston Villa, he said: "After 35 years in football I am quite lucky that I have seen many things. I was lucky to play three or four years with [Alessandro] Del Piero, [Zinedine] Zidane -- they don't remember because they were very young -- and Rayan has many good things but it's just a matter of balance.

"I like it when the players are happy, 100%, but I also like simple things, don't complicate it.

"Sometimes when players are so good like Rayan, they need to do that and when he does that I know he is happy, and if he can create chances for the team it is even better.

"This is something he needs to keep. He loves the ball, he wants the ball, and this is not something I am going to remove.

"But we need to find the right balance as when we can contact him in the right position, he can create chances."

stories.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Notable names you can bench in tough matchups this week
stories.summary: With important sit-or-start decisions ahead, Michael lists key starters you should think about benching.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 22: Notable names you can bench in Week 7
By Michael F. Florio

Deciding whether or not to sit one of your big-name options is the toughest decision in fantasy football. Here are some big names you can consider sitting this week and some options you can start instead.

Patrick Mahomes has scored fewer than 18 fantasy points in three straight games, including just 10.5 last week. The Kansas City Chiefs rushing attack is so effective that it has hurt Mahomes' fantasy value, keeping him to 30 passes or fewer in the past three games. He also gets the Seattle Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest passing yards in the NFL. Sit Mahomes for the names listed above, as well as Tyler Shough and Aaron Rodgers. I would also sit Xavier Worthy.
Dak Prescott has scored fewer than 13 fantasy points in back-to-back games. Not only that, but he has topped 19 fantasy points only once this season, which came in a great matchup against the Washington Commanders. In each of the past four games he has just one touchdown. He faces the Philadelphia Eagles, who held him to one TD pass per game last season. This also could be a lower-scoring divisional matchup. I would sit him for Jordan Love, C.J. Stroud, Bryce Young and Kyler Murray if you have them.
While I do not think fantasy managers can sit them, I do want to warn that Chuba Hubbard and Ashton Jeanty could disappoint this week. Jeanty, who was out touched by Mike Washington Jr in the second half last week, faces the Los Angeles Rams who have allowed just two touchdowns to running backs. Hubbard faces the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who have allowed the second-fewest rushing yards per game, just two rushing touchdowns and the fifth-fewest fantasy PPG.
Cam Skattebo did not have a touch in Week 6. I do think he will earn touches back, but it is likely he is in a split at best. The New York Giants could opt to use three backs. Regardless, it is a tough matchup against the Houston Texans who have allowed the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game to RBs. Sit him for Woody Marks, J.K. Dobbins, Ollie Gordon II and even Dameon Pierce.
Sit Tony Pollard against the Cleveland Browns. He has seen volume on the ground, but has only two targets and no catches in the past two games. He is more of a floor play and floors are lowered in tough matchups. The Browns have allowed just one rush touchdown and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.
Unfortunately, my guy TreVeyon Henderson should be sat against the Bears, who have allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy PPG to RBs. The New England Patriots could be using three backs once again. Henderson also is dealing with an ankle injury that could hurt his explosiveness, which is his best attribute.
Get away from the Indianapolis Colts' pass catchers this week. The Vikings have allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy PPG to wide receivers, including just three touchdowns against four interceptions on passes to the position. They have allowed the second-fewest fantasy PPG and no touchdowns to tight ends. Fantasy managers should try to get away from Tyler Warren, who is not a lock to play due to injury. They should certainly sit Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

Monangai out for "Thursday Night Football"

Kyle Monangai, Chicago Bears, RB (thumb/toe): Monangai is out for "Thursday Night Football." This is his third game missed, and in the prior two, D'Andre Swift went for at least 70 yards in each with a total of three touchdowns. He is a must play option given how beat up the RB position is. For those in need of a streamer, Roschon Johnson is an option. He has played about 40% of the snaps with Monangai sidelined. Last week he had 15 opportunities and the week prior he had seven targets. He should remain involved with it being a short week. -Florio

Oct. 21: J.J. McCarthy named Giants' starting QB for Week 7

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

The inevitable has finally arrived in New York: McCarthy is reportedly going to start at quarterback for the Giants in Week 7.

It was a decision destined to happen at some point following McCarthy's Sept. 28 acquisition from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick. And it was a decision almost assuredly destined to happen this week after the Michigan product delivered 16.52 fantasy points in the fourth quarter alone, nearly leading his Giants to a comeback from down 34-10 to the Saints.

McCarthy's installation doesn't promise any miracles, not for the Giants and not for fantasy, but it's an understandable, aggressive move that could positively shift the team's offensive dynamic.

First off, don't take McCarthy's Week 6 performance remotely to heart, as it's almost entirely meaningless for evaluative purposes. High-scoring relief efforts by quarterbacks aren't uncommon. Since 2021, there have been 13 relief performances of 15 or more fantasy points by quarterbacks who made a start later in that season; that group averaged 5.2 fewer fantasy points as starters than in that relief appearance.

More relevant to McCarthy's cause is his extensive tape from his 10 mediocre (to say it gently) starts in Minnesota last season. In those starts, he was 28th in Total QBR (36.1), 30th in completion rate (57.6%), 28th in off-target rate (19.3%) and 30th in touchdown-to-interception ratio (0.9). He struggled mightily when throwing into crowded spaces, with the fourth-worst passer rating when targeting a receiver with three or fewer yards of separation, per Next Gen Stats.

What McCarthy did do that could have fantasy relevance, however, was aim deep about as often as any quarterback in the league. His average depth of target of 8.8 yards led all quarterbacks who started at least half of their teams' games, though he did have seven interceptions on throws of at least 15 yards, putting his skill set into the extreme risk/reward category. Anyone who watched Sunday's game can attest to that, as McCarthy was chucking the ball in a desperate attempt to breathe some life into a Giants offense that, to that point, had shown barely any.

Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely each scored more than half of their Week 6 fantasy points after McCarthy entered the game, and the two combined for five catches on six targets for 130 yards and a touchdown on throws of at least 10 yards from McCarthy. Simply put, the upside is higher for both receivers with McCarthy under center, and that's especially relevant in a week with four teams on bye and the Giants facing an actually strong matchup against the Houston Texans defense. It's the fifth-most favorable matchup for wide receivers, when adjusted for the schedule.

Beyond those occasional highlight moments, also expect some ugly days for McCarthy, Nabers, Likely and anyone from the Giants' offense, depending on the quarterback's play, the matchups themselves and the current state of the running game. Cam Skattebo's last-minute role reduction (six snaps, no touches) thrust the offense into chaos last week, so we'll see how that plays out this week.

I've got McCarthy as my No. 21 quarterback in Week 7, which is a borderline superflex/2QB starter, though his upside could make him a stronger situational option than, say, Kirk Cousins against the Los Angeles Rams, if your lineup demands that.

NFL Nation: Adonai Mitchell returns to Jets practice

By Rich Cimini

The Jets' WR, sidelined the last four games with an injured finger on his right hand, returned to practice Wednesday on a limited basis -- his first practice since Sept. 25. His availability for Sunday against the Dolphins is a "pain tolerance issue," according to head coach Aaron Glenn. During the brief media period at practice, Mitchell seemed reluctant to use his right hand on one pass play in particular. If he's active for the game, he'd probably join Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr. in three-receiver sets.

Oct. 21: Are TEs more productive on National Tight Ends Day?

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

A note to Brock Bowers, Sam LaPorta, Juwan Johnson and all fellow tight ends: On Sunday, stand up and celebrate! It's National Tight Ends Day!

To their fantasy managers: You can all sit down. There's not much to see here.

Formally adopted as an NFL "holiday" beginning in 2019, National Tight Ends Day occurs on the fourth Sunday of October, as a way of honoring the position. This year, there is a 12-game slate on that day. Surely there'll be additional attention to the position on the highlight reel. For example, last season, Tucker Kraft and George Kittle celebrated their day with touchdowns, bringing it additional attention.

But from a fantasy perspective, historically speaking, National Tight Ends Day doesn't specifically inflate tight ends' production, at least not to decidedly actionable levels.

In the past seven seasons it has been celebrated (2019-25), tight end production was up only 0.29 fantasy points per game on October's fourth Sunday relative to the rest of the season, a differential as easily explained by random variance as by any additional boost provided by the now-annual event. Additionally, tight end usage was nearly identical to the numbers across the rest of the season, from routes run to target rate to red zone target rate to touchdowns scored.

There's only one area where a benefit seems apparent recently. Across the past three seasons, tight ends rostered in more than half of ESPN leagues at the time of National Tight Ends Day saw a boost of 3.65 fantasy points per game relative to the rest of their seasons. This was almost entirely due to the group seeing a noticeable, 17% boost in red zone target production, resulting in their touchdown rates more than doubling (0.66 per game, compared to 0.31 the rest of the season).

The small sample caveat naturally applies, since this was a group of 38 tight ends across three seasons. Additionally, across that same group, only three of their 40 best single-game totals from 2023-25 came on National Tight Ends Day. Is it possible that prominent tight ends are experiencing increasingly greater usage and attention on National Tight Ends Day as the holiday gains exposure across the league? Perhaps, and it's certainly something we're monitoring.

Is it something we should account for in our fantasy lineup planning? Well, no, not necessarily.

That said, if you're more moved by the data points, or if you're facing a razor-thin call at your flex spot between a tight end and a slightly more favorably projected running back or wide receiver, leaning tight end isn't an outrageous idea. Starting Mark Andrews (projected for 8.8 fantasy points in a favorable matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals) over Rome Odunze (projected for 10.2 in a less-ideal matchup against the New England Patriots) is a defensible move. Perhaps Lamar Jackson -- or Tyler Huntley, if Jackson is again out for Week 7 -- might choose to "celebrate" the occasion by giving Andrews that one additional red zone look he needs to hit paydirt.

Aside from that, sit back, enjoy the day, and here's hoping we see a third straight 20-point Isaiah Likely game and continued fantasy TE1 production from Kyle Pitts Sr., regardless of what the calendar tells us!

Oct. 20: Need RB help? Coleman set to return from IR this week

By Jeff Legwold, NFL Nation Broncos reporter

It will pay to keep an eye on the transactions this week, as the Denver Broncos are expected to activate rookie RB Jonah Coleman (19.8% rostered in ESPN leagues) from injured reserve. Coleman was the back of choice when the Broncos wanted to close out their Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, the same game in which he injured an ankle. Coleman has just the kind of decisiveness with the ball the Broncos need in the their run game right now. He will get some red zone carries because of his ability to break tackles, and he's a quality pass protector, so he'll get third-down snaps, as well.

Oct. 20: McLaurin, Evans leave MNF with injuries

By Michael F. Florio

Injuries were, unfortunately, the main story on Monday night. Terry McLaurin left early in the game as a result of a knee injury. He had to be carted off the field wearing an air cast. He seems likely to miss significant time. Mike Evans exited late in the first half -- after recording three catches for 94 yards -- due to an Achilles injury. Evans had been playing through this injury for the last couple of weeks. It seems likely he'll miss some time to allow this injury to heal.

The Evans injury led to more volume for the 49ers' stars. Both Christian McCaffrey (10) and George Kittle (8) had a season-high in targets. Both were already weekly must-starts but this added volume means even more production in fantasy.
Even without McLaurin, Jayden Daniels remains a weekly must-start. One week after running for over 100 yards and two touchdowns, he threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns. He has now scored at least 19 fantasy points in 17 out of his 22 career full games (77%). One thing to watch, however? He's been sacked nine times over the last two weeks.
Stefon Diggs saw seven targets on Monday night, going for 44 yards and a touchdown. He should see a boost in both targets and fantasy value as the top option for Daniels.
Chig Okonkwo is worth adding off the waiver wire for those streaming tight end. He saw seven targets, catching all of them for 69 yards. He led the Commanders in both catches and yards. His targets have increased each game this season and he may just be the No. 2 target for Daniels moving forward.
Treylon Burks left the game late. The Commanders are banged up at WR, meaning more volume could also go the way of Antonio Williams. Williams is worth a flier in 12-team leagues or deeper.
Rachaad White played on 71% of snaps, with seven carries and five targets. He turned that into 57 yards, a touchdown and 15.7 fantasy points. He is in play as an RB2 or flex option weekly with Jacory Croskey-Merritt on IR.
After averaging 27.0 fantasy PPG over the season's first three weeks, Brock Purdy has cooled off averaging just 17.7 FPPG over the last three weeks. He still has been an extremely safe option and gets a bounceback opportunity next week against the Atlanta Falcons, who have allowed the third-most passing yards.

Time to cut your Chargers?

So, you drafted a Charger and are not sure what to do with them heading into the team's bye week?

Many of them are droppable, starting with Justin Herbert. He has not reached 14 fantasy points in any game this season and is currently the overall QB25. Numerous QBs who have missed multiple games (Lamar Jackson, Daniels, Michael Penix Jr) have scored more fantasy points that Herbert. The only place I wouldn't let him go is in a superflex league, where all starting QBs are rostered.

The toughest decision is with Omarion Hampton. He's a talented back with double-digit touches in every game. It's hard to give up on this kind of player. The issue is that the Chargers are splitting their snaps in thirds between their three RBs. The Chargers' interior offensive line is struggling to create running lanes and the offense, as a whole, is struggling to create consistent scoring opportunities.

I have a lot of shares of Hampton but, as tempting as it has been, I have not yet dropped him. In 12-team leagues or deeper, you have no choice but to hold on. In 10-team leagues, it comes down to your RB depth. I played Rachaad White over Hampton in one league this week, which is making me question why I haven't dropped him. Still, after looking over the waiver wire, there's simply more upside in holding onto Hampton.

Ladd McConkey is the other question. McConkey has been extremely banged up and has left early in all but one game this season. I still believe in the talent -- and the bye week should (hopefully) allow him to get healthy. Please? I'm not ready to give up on McConkey and would keep him. However, the rest of the Chargers can be dropped if you're in need of finding a bye week replacement.

Of course, in most leagues, waivers don't run until early Wednesday morning. Spend today trying to trade any of these guys in exchange for a player you may like more than what's available on the waiver wire. Who knows? There may just be a manager in your league who still believes in a big name like Herbert.

Oct. 19: How Davante Adams injury affects Rams offense

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

The news on Davante Adams' injury suffered Sunday is devastating, as Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said Monday that the veteran wide receiver has a ruptured hamstring and will miss 6 to 10 weeks. Adams is the No. 7 wide receiver in fantasy points (102.0, or 17.0 per game), and he had been a top-10 weekly scorer in three of his first five games.

A 6-to-10 week timetable effectively ends Adams' fantasy regular season, as the midpoint of that range would take us through Week 14, directly before standard league playoffs begin. Though most leagues offer IR spots in which he could be stashed, steering through the bye weeks while keeping him there -- even if you're granted two or more of them -- isn't easy to do. If you need roster flexibility for bye weeks or injury fill-ins, it's reasonable to drop Adams in order to seek replacements. For now, try to keep him stashed there once he's officially moved to injured reserve, considering his past production and fantasy playoffs utility. The Rams have an extremely favorable Week 15 matchup for the position (DAL), as one example.

In Adams' absence, the Rams' offense takes a noticeable hit, as Adams and fellow Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua had accounted for 42% of the team's total targets for the season, and that's despite Nacua having missed two games due to a groin injury. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and Jordan Whittington will all likely see expanded roles while Adams is out, with Mumpfied the closest to fantasy relevant and more so in 12-team leagues with deep benches or 14-plus-team formats. Be aware, however, that those three totaled 12 targets and 24.4 fantasy points during Nacua's Weeks 2-3 absences, reflecting their low priority in the receiving pecking order.

It's the Rams' tight ends who should benefit most while Adams heals, as was the case in those same Weeks 2-3 games. Terrance Ferguson scored 17.4 fantasy points on nine targets in Week 2, before injuring his MCL in Week 3 and landing on IR. Tyler Higbee emerged with 20.2 fantasy points on 11 targets in Week 3, and he has now averaged 12.4 points and 6.8 targets in the past four weeks. Higbee is a definite add in any league larger than ESPN's standard, and Ferguson, who is eligible to return in Week 8, could warrant similar appeal if he's ready to play a week from now.

Stafford, meanwhile, will probably be more matchup dependent while Adams is sidelined. The veteran quarterback has been hit-or-miss for much of the season to date, but he'd offer his best fantasy utility for what align as favorable matchups in Weeks 9 (WSH), 10 (@ARI) and 15 (DAL).

Oct. 19: Who got the ball on Sunday?

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Woody Marks led the Texans backfield in snaps, routes run and touches in Week 6 with David Montgomery out. He finished with 81 total yards and 10.1 fantasy points against a tough Jaguars run defense. Jawhar Jordan scored on a 25-yard run but played a limited role behind Marks. Marks has now handled at least 15 carries in consecutive games. If Montgomery remains out, Marks is on the RB2 radar against the Giants in Week 7.

Marvin Harrison Jr. ranked fifth among Texans wide receivers in snaps and routes run in his team debut, behind Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Kayshon Boutte. He primarily lined up at Z receiver and may need time to adjust to Houston's offense. The Texans also have the fourth-easiest remaining schedule for fantasy wide receivers, which should benefit Harrison as he gets more comfortable in the offense and looks to rebuild the chemistry with C.J. Stroud, his college quarterback for two years at Ohio State.

Bhayshul Tuten finished with 16 touches, 87 total yards, two touchdowns and a season-high 24.7 fantasy points in Week 6. He led the Jaguars backfield in snaps and routes run despite Chris Rodriguez Jr. seeing more early-down work. Tuten also caught all four of his targets and has topped 80 total yards in four straight games. He remains a solid RB2 with RB1 upside following Jacksonville's Week 7 bye.

Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons

Drake London scored just 12.2 fantasy points, but his usage remains strong. He led Atlanta's pass catchers in targets (10), snaps and routes, and narrowly missed a long touchdown because of an inaccurate throw from Michael Penix Jr. There's no reason to worry about his WR1 status.

Kyle Pitts Sr. finished with a season-high seven targets and 23.0 fantasy points. More importantly, his playing time increased significantly after a limited role through the first five weeks. If that trend continues, Pitts could become a reliable weekly TE1. The Falcons also have the easiest remaining schedule for fantasy tight ends.

D'Andre Swift finished with 20 touches and 23.0 fantasy points, his second-highest total of the season. He led the Bears' backfield in snaps, routes, touches and fantasy points, while Roschon Johnson essentially filled Kyle Monangai's role. It's also worth mentioning that Chicago has the second-easiest remaining schedule for fantasy running backs. Both Swift and Monangai are worth targeting in trades.

Luther Burden III caught all eight of his targets for a season-high 95 yards, but his playing time remains a concern. He ran the sixth-most routes on the team despite being targeted on 44% of them. Burden also played a season-low number of snaps, with Kalif Raymond continuing to cut into his opportunities. More competitive games should help Burden see the field more, but for now, he's a boom-or-bust flex option.

Baltimore Ravens at Cleveland Browns

Jaleel McLaughlin led the Browns backfield in snaps and routes run in Week 6 while Quinshon Judkins was sidelined. He split carries evenly with Audric Estime but handled the receiving work, finishing with 13 touches and 9.5 fantasy points. Estime scored a rushing touchdown. Judkins could return in Week 7, but if he remains out, Dylan Sampson would be the preferred waiver pickup if activated.

Jerry Jeudy led Browns wide receivers with 10.9 fantasy points in Week 6, but Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion remain the better fantasy options. Both outpaced Jeudy in snaps, routes run and targets against the Ravens. Cleveland faces a Titans defense in Week 7 that ranks inside the top 15 in fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers. The Browns also have the 11th-easiest remaining schedule at the position.

Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts

Carnell Tate continues to lead the Titans in snaps, routes run and targets, including Week 6 against the Colts. He has a team-high 44 targets and has scored at least 11 fantasy points in three of his last four games, including two with 19 or more. Wan'Dale Robinson played a season-low snap share and is droppable in shallower leagues. Tennessee also has the fifth-easiest remaining schedule for fantasy wide receivers.

New York Jets at New England Patriots

A.J. Brown was heavily involved in his first game back after missing four games with a high ankle sprain. He played more than 75% of the offensive snaps and led the Patriots with 10 targets while also running the most routes. However, Brown had a career-high three drops and finished with just 5.7 fantasy points.

DeMario Douglas caught seven of eight targets for 19.6 fantasy points. He has now scored at least 19 fantasy points in consecutive games, but his playing time remains a concern. Douglas continues to see limited snaps and routes because he's primarily used in three-receiver sets. That makes it difficult to count on consistent production, especially with Brown back in the lineup. Romeo Doubs' shoulder injury could create more opportunities, but Douglas remains a risky flex option who's worth adding in deeper leagues.

Omar Cooper Jr. finished with seven targets and 22.3 fantasy points in his first game back from an ankle injury. He led the Jets in targets while playing extensively in both two- and three-receiver sets. Garrett Wilson still led the team in snaps and routes, but Cooper's role is worth watching. Adonai Mitchell's eventual return could cut into his playing time, but Cooper should be a priority waiver-wire target.

Braelon Allen led the Jets backfield in snaps, routes, touches (19) and fantasy points (12.4). He has at least 19 touches in consecutive games with Breece Hall sidelined. That kind of workload should continue to benefit Allen, who has a great matchup in Week 7 against a Dolphins defense allowing the fourth-most fantasy points per game to running backs. Allen should be viewed as a high-end RB2 as long as Hall remains out.

New Orleans Saints at New York Giants

Kendre Miller led the Saints' backfield in snaps and touches, finishing with 20 carries for 70 yards and 9.0 fantasy points. Alvin Kamara entered the game with a back injury and finished with 14.9 fantasy points, but he had just nine touches and didn't play in the fourth quarter. CJ Donaldson continued to handle passing-down work. Miller is worth picking up in all leagues and could be a flex option against the Steelers in Week 7 if Kamara remains limited.

Isaiah Likely continues to see plenty of opportunities in the Giants' passing game. Only Malachi Fields played more snaps among New York's pass catchers, and only Malik Nabers (15) had more targets than Likely (11). Likely has now seen at least 11 targets in three straight games and scored at least 23 fantasy points in two of them. He belongs in fantasy lineups as a TE1 against the Texans in Week 7.

Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles

Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan have emerged as Carolina's 1A and 1B receivers. Coker led the team with 13 targets, finishing with 97 yards and 15.7 fantasy points. McMillan had 86 yards and 14.6 points while leading the team in snaps and routes. Both are averaging at least 17 fantasy points and eight targets per game this season. They're weekly fantasy starters, but Carolina's difficult remaining schedule for wide receivers makes both worth considering as candidates to trade away.

Chuba Hubbard continues to play significant snaps and run a high number of routes with Jonathon Brooks sidelined and AJ Dillon also missing Week 6. He finished with 19.1 fantasy points, and this was his sixth career game with at least 100 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown. Hubbard has at least 21 touches in three straight games, including a season-high 29 against the Eagles. With that kind of workload, Hubbard remains a must-start for fantasy managers.

Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Jaylen Warren remained the Steelers' lead back with Rico Dowdle returning from a three-game absence. Warren finished with 16 touches for 78 total yards and 9.8 fantasy points, while Dowdle had 10 touches for 49 yards and 7.9 points. Warren handled most of the third-down work and took on a larger role in the fourth quarter and overtime. He remains an RB2, while Dowdle is difficult to trust outside of deeper leagues.

Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams

Tyler Allgeier led Arizona's backfield in snaps, routes and touches (19) with Jeremiyah Love sidelined by an ankle injury but finished with just 5.8 fantasy points. Bam Knight was much more productive, turning 17 touches into 11.8 points. Knight also earned more opportunities as the game progressed. If Love misses Week 7, Knight could be the better fantasy option, assuming his wrist is fine. Allgeier should remain involved in short-yardage and passing situations.

Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs

Xavier Worthy led the Chiefs in snaps, routes and targets with Rashee Rice sidelined. He caught all seven targets for 14.3 fantasy points. Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong saw increased playing time but combined for just four receptions and 37 yards. Worthy has now scored at least 11 fantasy points in two straight games. Worthy should continue seeing a ton of opportunities as long as Rice is sidelined, making him a flex option with WR2 upside.

Omarion Hampton led the Chargers' backfield in snaps, routes, touches (11) and fantasy points (7.9), but Kimani Vidal wasn't far behind with 10 touches. Keaton Mitchell also saw playing time. It's hard to trust any of these running backs right now, especially with Los Angeles ranking 26th in total yards and 30th in points scored per game. The Chargers have a bye in Week 7, and changes to the backfield rotation wouldn't be surprising.

Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders

Ashton Jeanty finished with 15.8 fantasy points, but his snap rate has dropped noticeably over the past two weeks compared to the first four games of the season. He handled just 10 carries for 22 yards and a touchdown, adding four receptions for 36 yards. Mike Washington Jr. continues to cut into his early-down work as Jeanty deals with a foot injury. Jeanty remains a fantasy starter, but his reduced workload limits his RB1 upside.

Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers

Pierre Strong Jr. led the Packers' backfield in snaps, routes and touches (16), finishing with 11.7 fantasy points. MarShawn Lloyd had just 10 rushing yards on eight carries and briefly left the game with an injury. Josh Jacobs is expected to return from the commissioner's exempt list ahead of Week 7 and could eventually take back the lead role. Strong could still get work on passing downs, but Lloyd will be difficult to trust in fantasy lineups.

stories.headline: Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win
stories.summary: Como head coach Cesc Fàbregas said he regrets telling his players to ease off towards the end of their famous 4-1 win against misfiring Manchester United.
stories.body:
Como head coach Cesc Fàbregas said he regrets telling his players to ease off towards the end of their famous 4-1 win against misfiring Manchester United.

The Champions League upstarts heaped pressure on Red Devils boss Michael Carrick by swatting aside the three-time European champions with ease on Wednesday evening.

Nico Paz marked a sparkling man-of-the-match display with a brace at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, where Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramón also struck for the ever-improving Serie A side.

But Fàbregas' pride in the performance was tinged by disappointment at seeing United substitute Joshua Zirkzee score a stoppage-time consolation, admitting he turned his attention to Saturday's match against Sassuolo during the closing stages.

"I believe that tactically speaking the team played a rather good game," the former Arsenal and Chelsea star said.

"I regret maybe the last 10 minutes when I was the one telling the team to slow down the pace because there was another game and maybe with a 4-0 lead they could have managed something.

"I told Tasos Douvikas not to run anymore, to stay in the middle and maybe that is what I regret, because I'm the first one who always pushes the fight until the end. That goal hurt me."

stories.headline: Party like it's 1982? What baseball looked like during Brewers' last World Series
stories.summary: It's been a long, long wait for Milwaukee fans to see their team play again on baseball's biggest stage in October.
stories.body:
It's time for Milwaukee to party like it's 1982.

On Friday, for the first time in 44 years, the Milwaukee Brewers will play in the World Series. Back then, the club's search for its first-ever pennant didn't last too long -- the Brewers won the American League just 12 years after starting play in Milwaukee. (The Brewers moved to the National League in 1998.) But after a seven-game series loss to the St. Louis Cardinals, a drought in the quest to make it back to the sport's final stage ensued.

Milwaukee has emerged as one of Major League Baseball's most consistent organizations in recent years. The Brewers have won five of the last six National League Central titles, and haven't dipped below 85 wins in a full season since 2016. However, they weren't able to win out over the rest of the NL's best come postseason time.

Until this year.

The Brewers stormed through the National League's playoff bracket in dominant fashion, dispatching the San Diego Padres three games to one before sweeping the Los Angeles Dodgers, a fittingly impressive run for a team that boasted the best regular-season record in the majors.

As a result, World Series baseball is back on the Wisconsin shores of Lake Michigan for the first time in nearly four and a half decades. Unsurprisingly, things have changed quite a bit around baseball since the Brewers last played in the Fall Classic.

Here's a look at what baseball and the other major U.S. sports looked like back in 1982.

Yount, Thomas and more lead the way for 'Harvey's Wallbangers'
The 1982 edition of the Brewers came with a memorable nickname: Harvey's Wallbangers, a play off a popular cocktail referencing the name of Brewers manager Harvey Kuenn and the squad's power-hitting bona fides. Kuenn didn't become manager until midseason, taking over in an interim capacity after Buck Rodgers was dismissed with the team sitting at .500 two months into the season. Kuenn got the team into second gear, and Milwaukee would win the AL East on the season's final day.

The key ingredient in the Brewers' surge? Home runs. Milwaukee clobbered 216 that season, 30 more than the next closest team. Among the team's leaders were Gorman Thomas (39), Ben Oglivie (34) and Cecil Cooper (32), with a trio of future Hall of Famers right behind in Robin Yount (29), Ted Simmons (23) and Paul Molitor (19). 1982 was a particularly stellar year for Yount, who won two of his career MVP awards and led the league in hits and slugging percentage.

Other league leaders
While Yount took home the American League's Most Valuable Player honors, the National League's award went to Dale Murphy of the Atlanta Braves. Murphy clubbed 36 home runs, led the NL in runs batted in and added a Gold Glove in the field for good measure -- and he'd win the award again in 1983, becoming just the ninth player to win the award back to back.

On the mound, in the NL, 37-year-old Steve Carlton delivered the final of his four Cy Young-winning seasons, recording a major-league-best 23 wins and 286 strikeouts on a MLB-high 295⅔ total innings pitched. On the American League side, another Brewer came home with high honors, as Pete Vuckovich won the league's Cy Young, amassing an impressive 18-6 record.

Clubs and alignment younger fans may not recognize
Did the earlier reference to the Brewers being in the American League throw you off? Well, there's plenty more where that came from. Major League Baseball in 1982 did not exactly mirror the sport we see today. Instead of three divisions of five teams per league, it was two divisions of seven in the American League ... and two divisions of six in the National League. Alignment accordingly was wacky -- the Detroit Tigers were in the AL East with the Brewers for instance, while the 1982 National League West winner was ... the not-particularly-western Atlanta Braves.

The teams weren't a one-to-one match to the modern day, either. The California Angels won the AL West that season, pre-dating future name changes to the Anaheim Angels, Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim and Los Angeles Angels. Meanwhile in the NL East, the Montreal Expos were alive and well, with the club's eventual relocation to Washington, D.C., still decades away.

Around the rest of the sporting world
While the Cardinals took the 1982 World Series home to St. Louis, the rest of the 1982-83 sports calendar would belong to the northeast in other major American sports.

Washington would be the first northeastern city to grab a title in the ensuing months, as its dominant NFL squad steamrolled the league to a 12-1 record and a Super Bowl crown in January 1983. New York was next in May, with the New York Islanders powering their way to a Stanley Cup Final sweep of the Edmonton Oilers, before the title luck headed back down I-95 to Philadelphia for the NBA Finals just days later -- the 76ers swept the Los Angeles Lakers in that year's championship series.

stories.headline: Stanley Cup odds: Central-leading Mammoth see odds shorten after hot start
stories.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes are favorites to win the 2027 Stanley Cup while other teams drop after three weeks.
stories.body:
Since their inaugural season in 2024-25, the Utah Mammoth have continued to gain momentum as a franchise and bookmakers took notice, assigning them the 14th-best Stanley Cup odds going into the 2026-27 campaign at 30-1. Now, after a strong start to the season that has them leading the Central Division at 7-3-0, the Mammoth are 19-1 for the Cup.

Because the Mammoth are not a naturally popular team, and Utah is not state with legal betting, they haven't attracted as much attention as Caesars Sportsbook head of hockey Karry Shreeve thinks they should, though it's more than in previous seasons.

"Utah is finally starting to get a little bit more public traction," he told ESPN before the season. "Those odds aren't going to demand the same attention as some of those other teams would. So, I think like anything else ... there could be value on Utah as the season goes along for some of the future stuff anyways."

The reigning champion Carolina Hurricanes lead the pack of Stanley Cup contenders and have shortened from +650 to +600 since the start of the season. The Tampa Bay Lightning (10-1 to +800) and Washington Capitals (17-1 to 11-1) continue to improve with strong performances, while the Florida Panthers have lengthened from +650 to +850 since the start of the campaign after being one of the buzziest teams of the offseason.

stories.headline: Ranking the greatest players in WNBA history, from A'ja Wilson to Becky Hammon
stories.summary: Before the WNBA's 30th season wraps up, ESPN voted on the league's all-time greatest players. There's a new No. 1.
stories.body:
As the WNBA Finals wrap up the league's 30th season, it's time for one of the hardest countdowns: ranking the top 30 players in WNBA history.

No. 1 shouldn't be a surprise, even if she just missed being on ESPN's top-25 list for the league's 25th anniversary in 2021: A'ja Wilson's past five years have been extraordinary.

We surveyed WNBA experts from across ESPN; 23 voters sent in ballots, with the top 30 vote-getters making the list.

It's always difficult to evaluate careers from different eras, and the talent pool keeps growing with the league. Which players from the WNBA's earlier years perpetually stay in this kind of ranking, and which might be replaced?

In 2021, two players who already won MVP awards still did not make our top 25. Now, though, the Las Vegas Aces' Wilson has jumped to the top spot, and the New York Liberty's Jonquel Jones is No. 27. Both have won WNBA titles since 2021; Wilson, in fact, has since won three championships, and also is now a five-time MVP.

No ranking will satisfy everyone, but these 30 players -- including seven who competed in the 2026 season -- stood out the most for our panel as the best ever.

More:

Snubs and other overlooked players | Voting panel

1. A'ja Wilson
C | Las Vegas Aces (2018-present)

Career stats: 26.2 PPG, 9.4 RPG, 1.9 BPG

Highlights (17 first-place votes): Three championships (2022, 2023, 2025); five-time MVP (2020, 2022, 2023, 2025, 2026); two-time Finals MVP (2023, 2025); three-time Defensive Player of the Year; five-time All-Defensive first team; three-time scoring champ; career scoring average leader (22.05); five-time All-WNBA first team; Commissioner's Cup champion (2022)

Wilson was the most debated player left off our 2021 list, primarily because she had been in the WNBA for only four seasons then. She has won four of her five MVPs since and overwhelmingly claimed the No. 1 ranking. Aces coach Becky Hammon jokes that she has nearly exhausted her list of compliments for Wilson, but she will have to keep working on it. Wilson, who turned 30 in August, still has more great basketball to come. -- Michael Voepel

2. Diana Taurasi

G | Phoenix Mercury (2004-24)

Career stats: 18.8 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 4.2 APG

Highlights (five first-place votes): Three championships (2007, 2009, 2014); MVP (2009); two-time Finals MVP (2009, 2014); all-time leading scorer (only player over 10,000 points); five-time scoring champ; 10-time All-WNBA first team

Think of any basketball superlative and it applies to Taurasi. Tough. A winner. Clutch. Unrelenting. Brilliant as a shooter, passer and playmaker. She won big. She scored big. She played big. She has always been the player no one could take their eyes off of. Don't turn away because something great could happen. To say she was born with the "clutch gene" is to greatly undersell just how good Taurasi was at the end of games. That Taurasi is the WNBA's all-time leading scorer -- and more than 2,000 points ahead of second-place Tina Charles -- is a testament to her sustained brilliance. -- Charlie Creme

3. Maya Moore

F | Minnesota Lynx (2011-18)

Career stats: 18.4 PPG, 5.9 RPG, 3.3 APG, 1.7 SPG, 45.3 FG%

Highlights: Four championships (2011, 2013, 2015, 2017); MVP (2014); Finals MVP (2013); Rookie of the Year (2011); one-time scoring champion; five-time All-WNBA first team; two-time All-Defensive team

Moore is the one player on this list for whom fans will forever ask, "What if?" Her career was short by superstar standards. But those eight years before she stepped away to help fight for criminal justice reform were just so good. Five times in that span she was the top scorer on a Lynx team that made the Finals six times and won four titles. Moore played with a smooth precision that looked like she was one step ahead of everyone, yet needing half the effort to do it. When Moore decided to step away from basketball after the 2018 season, she was still in her prime, one of the WNBA's best players, averaging 18.0 points and leading the league in steals, while earning All-WNBA second-team honors. -- Creme

4. Cynthia Cooper
G | Houston Comets (1997-2000, 2003)

Career stats: 21.0 PPG, 3.3 RPG, 4.9 APG, 45.9 FG%

Highlights (one first-place vote): Four championships (1997, 1998, 1999, 2000); two-time MVP (1997, 1998); four-time Finals MVP (1997, 1998, 1999, 2000); second in career scoring average (20.98 PPG); three-time scoring champion; four-time All-WNBA first team

Cooper has the shortest tenure -- only four full seasons -- of anyone on this list because she was already 34 when the league started. But her brilliant overseas career, mostly in Italy, helped her be ready to still excel in the WNBA. The new league needed a star to get it off the ground, and Cooper was that player. It seems serendipitous that the team Cooper made famous -- the Houston Comets -- returns next year after the 30th anniversary celebration this season. The Comets folded during the global financial crisis in 2008 but will be revived with the Connecticut Sun's relocation to Houston in 2027. -- Voepel

5. Lisa Leslie
C | Los Angeles Sparks (1997-2009)

Career stats: 17.3 PPG, 9.1 RPG, 2.4 APG, 47.0 FG%

Highlights: Two championships (2001, 2002); three-time MVP (2001, 2004, 2006); two-time Finals MVP (2001, 2002); 16th all time in scoring, eighth in rebounds, third in blocks; three-time rebounding champion; two-time Defensive Player of the Year; two-time All-Defensive first team; eight-time All-WNBA first team; first to dunk in a WNBA game

The Sparks just unveiled a statue of Leslie outside Crypto.com Arena in September, but her aura has never left the building. An original WNBA player along with Sheryl Swoopes and Rebecca Lobo, Leslie is one of the greatest centers in hoops history. At 25 when the WNBA launched, Leslie didn't have a league to play in for the first three years of her post-college prime. She also sat out one year on maternity leave. Still, Leslie finished with 12 exceptional seasons and was an All-WNBA selection her final year, shooting a career-high 51.8% from the field then. -- Voepel

6. Sheryl Swoopes

F/G | Houston Comets (1997-2007); Seattle Storm (2008); Tulsa Shock (2011)

Career stats: 15.0 PPG, 4.9 RPG, 3.2 APG, 2.0 SPG

Highlights: Four championships (1997, 1998, 1999, 2000); three-time MVP (2000, 2002, 2005); three-time Defensive Player of the Year (2000, 2002, 2003); two-time scoring champion and steals champion; five-time All-WNBA first team; seven-time All-Defensive team

Swoopes was as influential as she was great. In the early 2000s, Swoopes might have been considered the league's best offensive player and the best defensive player. In her first MVP season, she led the WNBA in scoring and steals. That came just as she was finishing up her run with Cynthia Cooper and Tina Thompson of four WNBA championships in the league's first four years. With Air Swoopes she was the first women's player with a signature shoe, launching just before the WNBA did. -- Creme

7. Tamika Catchings

F | Indiana Fever (2002-16)

Career stats: 16.1 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 3.3 APG, 2.4 SPG

Highlights: One championship (2012); MVP (2011); Finals MVP (2012); only player in WNBA history to rank in career top 10 in steals (first), points (third), rebounds (fourth) and assists (eighth); five-time Defensive Player of the Year; seven-time All-WNBA first team

Never taking anything for granted, Catchings played hard all the time. Effort meant as much to her as her immense talent. Catchings was a consistently aggressive rebounder and was a complete player. She is still the only player in league history to finish in the top 10 in points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks in the same season -- and she did it twice (2002 and 2006). She was fifth all time in playoff scoring and played even better in the postseason. She averaged 16.8 points in 68 career postseason games, and 19.0 points and 8.5 rebounds in the Fever's 2012 title run. -- Creme

8. Breanna Stewart

F | Seattle Storm (2016-22); New York Liberty (2023-present)

Career stats: 20.5 PPG, 8.5 RPG, 3.2 APG

Highlights: Three championships (2018, 2020, 2024); two-time MVP (2018, 2023); two-time Finals MVP (2018, 2020); Rookie of the Year (2016); three-time Commissioner's Cup champion (2021, 2023, 2026); two-time Commissioner's Cup MVP (2021, 2026); six-time All-WNBA first team; eight-time All-Defensive team

With her 6-4 frame and 7-1 wingspan to go along with guard-level ballhandling skills and deep shooting range, Stewart might be the most physically distinctive player the WNBA has ever seen. She runs the floor brilliantly but can also lead a break. There isn't a position on the court she can't guard or an area of the game she can't influence. Her two MVP awards only tell part of the story. Stewart has finished in the top three in MVP voting six times in the 10 seasons she has played (she missed 2019 because of an Achilles injury). -- Creme

9. Candace Parker
F/C | Los Angeles Sparks (2008-20); Chicago Sky (2021-22); Las Vegas Aces(2023)

Career stats: 16.0 PPG, 8.5 RPG, 4.0 APG, 1.5 BPG

Highlights: Three championships (2016, 2021, 2023); two-time MVP (2008, 2013); Finals MVP (2016); Rookie of the Year (2008); Defensive Player of the Year (2020); seven-time All-WNBA first team; fourth in career rebounds and fifth in blocks

Parker was a role model for the modern version of the multiposition player and is often mentioned when younger players are asked about their idols. Her biggest value was as a creative post with great hands and footwork, but Parker also could run the offense and facilitate like a point guard because of her superb court vision. Though the bulk of her career was with the Sparks, she won her last two championships with Chicago (her hometown team) and Las Vegas. -- Voepel

10. Lauren Jackson
F | Seattle Storm (2001-12)

Career stats: 18.9 PPG, 7.7 RPG, 1.4 APG, 46.0 FG%

Highlights: Two championships (2004, 2010); three-time MVP (2003, 2007, 2010); Finals MVP (2010); Defensive Player of the Year (2007); seven-time All-WNBA first team; two-time All-Defensive first team; three-time scoring champion

Jackson, the No. 1 pick in 2001 at age 19, wasn't the first Australian in the WNBA, but she remains her nation's best women's player. At 6-5, she could anchor the defense, be the offense's target in the paint and step outside and hit 3-pointers. Guarding Jackson was always a chore, since she was a scoring threat from anywhere. Injuries limited her WNBA career to 12 seasons, playing only 28 games combined (regular season and playoffs) over her last two years. But when healthy, she was as good as any post player in WNBA history. -- Voepel

11. Sue Bird
G | Seattle Storm (2002-22)

Career stats: 11.7 PPG, 2.5 RPG, 5.6 APG

Highlights: Four championships (2004, 2010, 2018, 2020); Commissioner's Cup champion (2021); career leader in games (580) and assists (3,234); second in career 3-pointers and third in steals; first player in WNBA history to win titles in three different decades; five-time All-WNBA first team

It might seem unfair that Bird isn't in the top 10, but it reflects something in which point guards take pride: making everyone around them better. The player right ahead of Bird on this list, longtime Storm teammate Lauren Jackson, would attest to that. No one played more WNBA games or was more respected as a leader than the Seattle icon, who has a statue outside Climate Pledge Arena. Though Bird is known for her facilitating, she also was a clutch scorer. Only her UConn and Olympic teammate Diana Taurasi made more 3-pointers in the WNBA. -- Voepel

12. Sylvia Fowles

C | Chicago Sky (2008-14); Minnesota Lynx (2015-22)

Career stats: 15.7 PPG, 9.8 RPG, 59.8 FG%

Highlights: Two championships (2015, 2017); MVP (2017); two-time Finals MVP (2015, 2017); second all time in rebounds; all-time leader in field goal percentage, fourth all time in blocks; four-time Defensive Player of the Year; three-time All-WNBA first team; 11-time All-Defensive team

Few players can control a game staying almost exclusively in the paint the way Fowles did. She was the quintessential traditional center. Fowles dominated the glass at both ends, influenced her opponents' shots just with her presence and only took shots she knew she could make. And she made plenty of them. Six times in her career, Fowles shot over 60% from the field. She led the league in rebounding three times and blocks twice. And it was all done quietly. No fanfare. No wild on-court emotions. Fowles was calm, cool and ruthless all at once. -- Creme

13. Elena Delle Donne
F/G | Chicago Sky (2013-16); Washington Mystics (2017-2023)

Career stats: 19.5 PPG, 6.7 RPG, 1.6 BPG, 93.7 FT%

Highlights: One championship (2019); two-time MVP (2015, 2019); Rookie of the Year (2013); first 50-40-90 season in WNBA history (2019); career leader in free throw percentage; one-time scoring champion; four-time All-WNBA first team

At 6-5, Delle Donne was an unstoppable scoring machine with the combination of her size and elite shooting ability from all over the court. Fouling her wasn't an option, either: Delle Donne is the best free throw shooter in league history, combining textbook form with cool nerves. She led the Mystics to their only WNBA title while playing through severe back pain that was later diagnosed as three herniated discs. Injuries and dealing with the long-term effects of Lyme disease shortened Delle Donne's career, but her impact was enormous. -- Voepel

14. Tina Thompson
F | Houston Comets (1997-2008); Los Angeles Sparks (2009-11); Seattle Storm (2012-13)

Career stats: 15.1 PPG, 6.2 RPG

Highlights: Four championships (1997, 1998, 1999, 2000); fifth all-time in scoring, seventh in 3-pointers made; three-time All-WNBA first team

Cynthia Cooper and Sheryl Swoopes are the players most associated with the Comets' four championships, but Thompson might have been the glue. When she retired in 2013, Thompson's 7,488 points were the most in league history. Perhaps nothing exemplifies Thompson's commitment more than her final season, when she was an All-Star while averaging 14.1 points in her 17th season. Forever the answer to a trivia question as the first college player drafted into the WNBA, Thompson was one of its foundational players, and her physicality and toughness set a standard for the league's future. -- Creme

15. Seimone Augustus
G/F | Minnesota Lynx (2006-19); Los Angeles Sparks (2020)

Career stats: 15.4 PPG, 3.1 RPG; 2.3 APG

Highlights: Four championships (2011, 2013, 2015, 2017); Finals MVP (2011); Rookie of the Year (2006); one-time All-WNBA first team

The No. 1 pick in 2006, Augustus was the foundation of the Lynx dynasty that was built around her. A huge part of Minnesota's success was how Augustus welcomed Maya Moore, the top pick in 2011, and never worried about being overshadowed. The team's results mattered most to Augustus, who was on the All-WNBA second team five times. A Baton Rouge, Louisiana, native who put LSU on the map in women's hoops, Augustus was known for having one of the WNBA's smoothest jump shots. -- Voepel

16. Nneka Ogwumike
F | Los Angeles Sparks (2012-23, 2026); Seattle Storm (2024-25)

Career stats: 16.8 PPG, 7.6 RPG, 53.7 FG%

Highlights: One championship (2016); MVP (2016); Rookie of the Year (2012); 11-time WNBA All-Star; third all-time leading rebounder; one-time All-WNBA first team (2016); four-time All-Defensive first team

Steadiness, both in play and personality, might be the simplest way to define a multifaceted professional basketball life. In a 15-year WNBA career that ended last month, Ogwumike never scored fewer than 12.6 points per game in a season. She was the sport's best player in 2016 with a historically efficient season (19.7 PPG on 66.5 FG%) and led the Sparks to a championship. She's undoubtedly an all-time great player, but Ogwumike's legacy will be tied just as much to the respect and admiration she earned throughout basketball. As president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association for 10 years, Ogwumike twice negotiated landmark collective bargaining agreements that helped change the league. -- Creme

17. Brittney Griner
C | Phoenix Mercury (2013-24); Atlanta Dream (2025); Connecticut Sun (2026-present)

Career stats: 16.6 PPG, 7.1 RPG, 2.4 BPG

Highlights: One championship (2014); all-time leader in blocks; two-time scoring champion (2017, 2019); eight-time blocks champion; career dunks leader; two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2014, 2015); three-time All-WNBA first team; six-time All-Defensive team; co-comeback player of the year (2023)

Defense will always be the first thing that comes to mind when reflecting on Griner's career. She has been the league's fiercest rim protector for nearly all her 14 years in the WNBA. But as Griner's offensive game developed, she became nearly as dominant at that end of the court. Her short turnaround jumper was impossible to stop when the 6-9 Griner was at her peak. Coming off one her best seasons in 2021, Griner's career, and the willingness of some players to continue playing overseas, was greatly impacted by her arrest and detainment in a Russian prison and penal colony for nearly 10 months in 2022. After missing one season, Griner remarkably recovered and came back to average 17.5 points in 2023 for the Mercury. -- Creme

18. Yolanda Griffith
C/F | Sacramento Monarchs (1999-2007), Seattle Storm (2008); Indiana Fever (2009)

Career stats: 13.6 PPG, 7.9 RPG, 1.7 SPG, 50.1 FG%

Highlights: One championship (2005); MVP (1999); Finals MVP (2005); Defensive Player of the Year (1999); two-time rebounding champion; two-time All-WNBA first team

Griffith wasn't well-known when she entered the WNBA at age 29 in 1999, having not played at the Division I level in college for personal reasons. But after several years playing overseas and then in the short-lived ABL, Griffith took the WNBA by storm in her first season, winning MVP and DPOY honors. The 6-4 center averaged a double-double in each of her first three WNBA seasons. She would be much higher on career lists had she been able to spend her entire pro career in the WNBA, but she made the most of her time in the league. -- Voepel

19. Tina Charles
C | Connecticut Sun (2010-13, 2025); New York Liberty (2014-19); Washington Mystics (2020-2021); Seattle Storm (2022); Phoenix Mercury (2022); Atlanta Dream (2024)

Career stats: 17.8 PPG, 9.0 RPG, 2.2 APG

Highlights: MVP (2012); Rookie of the Year (2010); WNBA all-time leading rebounder, second all time in scoring; two-time scoring champion; four-time rebounding champion; five-time All-WNBA first team; four-time All-Defensive team

A dominant force from the day she stepped onto a WNBA court, Charles was the epitome of reliability and productivity until her retirement in May. In her first season she led the Sun in scoring. In her final season, 16 years later, Charles led the Sun in scoring. Plenty happened in between, like grabbing more rebounds than anyone in league history or leading the WNBA in scoring in her 11th season (23.4 PPG for the Mystics in 2021). A title might have eluded Charles, but not much else did. -- Creme

20. Katie Smith
G | Minnesota Lynx (1999-2005); Detroit Shock (2005-09); Washington Mystics (2010); Seattle Storm (2011-12); New York Liberty (2013)

Career stats: 13.4 PPG, 2.9 RPG, 2.6 APG

Highlights: Two championships (2006, 2008); Finals MVP (2008); third in career 3-pointers; one-time scoring champion; two-time All-WNBA first team

After winning two ABL titles in Columbus, where she previously starred at Ohio State, Smith was allocated to the new Minnesota WNBA franchise in 1999. With the Lynx, she was best known as a scorer. Traded during the 2005 season to Detroit, Smith took over at point guard and helped lead the Shock to three consecutive trips to the WNBA Finals, winning two. She is the only one in the top 15 scorers in WNBA history who played in the ABL first. She also had the physicality to be a strong defender. -- Voepel

21. Lindsay Whalen
G | Connecticut Sun (2004-09); Minnesota Lynx (2010-18)

Career stats: 11.5 PPG; 4.9 APG, 3.8 RPG; 46.1 FG%
Highlights: Four championships (2011, 2013, 2015, 2017); fifth all time in assists; three-time assists champion; three-time All-WNBA first team

When Whalen decided to return home to Minnesota after six seasons in Connecticut, it changed the trajectory of her career, the fortunes of the Lynx franchise and the course of WNBA history. Whalen's ability to lead, distribute the basketball and make winning plays at key moments helped bring four championships in seven years to Minnesota. No player in league history was part of more playoff wins (54) than Whalen, whose 377 victories rank second to DeWanna Bonner. That both the Sun and Lynx have retired Whalen's No. 13 jersey is a testament to how much she meant to two franchises. -- Creme

22. Cappie Pondexter
G | Phoenix Mercury (2006-09); New York Liberty (2010-14), Chicago Sky (2015-17), Los Angeles Sparks (2018), Indiana Fever (2018)

Career stats: 16.4 PPG, 3.7 RPG, 3.8 APG

Highlights: Two championships (2007, 2009); Finals MVP (2007), three-time All-WNBA first team, ninth in career scoring

The No. 2 draft pick in 2006, Pondexter formed a strong backcourt with Diana Taurasi for four seasons in Phoenix, resulting in two WNBA titles. Pondexter was one of the league's most dynamic scorers, especially over the first 10 seasons of her career. Her best statistical season was her first in New York in 2010, when she averaged 21.4 points and shot 43% from 3-point range, both career bests. -- Voepel

23. Chelsea Gray
G | Connecticut Sun (2015); Los Angeles Sparks (2016-20); Las Vegas Aces (2019-present)

Career stats: 12.0 PPG, 3.2 RPG, 5.2 APG

Highlights: Four championships (2016, 2022, 2023, 2025); one finals MVP (2022); one all-WNBA first team (2019); seventh all time in assists

From role player on the Sparks' title team in 2016 to catalyst of three championships in Las Vegas, Gray is now one of the WNBA's all-time winners. Her leadership has been instrumental in the Aces' dynasty, but her fearlessness defines Gray's game, whether it's a thread-the-needle pass or willingness to take a big shot. Her 2022 Finals MVP was built on clock-beating jumpers, and she became the first player in WNBA history this season to hit a tying buzzer-beater to force overtime and then a winner in overtime in the same game to beat the Fever. -- Creme

24. Angel McCoughtry
F/G | Atlanta Dream (2009-19); Las Vegas Aces (2020-21), Minnesota Lynx (2022)

Career stats: 18.6 PPG, 5.0 RPG, 2.9 APG, 2.0 SPG

Highlights: Rookie of the Year (2009); 10th in career steals; two-time scoring leader and steals leader; two-time All-WNBA first team, six-time All-Defensive first team

The No. 1 pick in the 2009 draft, McCoughtry was a franchise-changing player for the Dream, who joined the WNBA in 2008. She led Atlanta to the WNBA Finals in 2010, 2011 and 2013, then also played in the Finals with Las Vegas in 2020. Few players in the league have combined elite scoring and defense as consistently as McCoughtry did. -- Voepel

25. Deanna Nolan
G | Detroit Shock (2001-09)

Career stats: 13.6 PPG, 3.8 RPG, 3.2 APG

Highlights: Three championships (2003, 2006, 2008); Finals MVP (2006); two-time All-WNBA first team; one-time All-Defensive first team

The No. 6 draft pick in 2001, Nolan was from Flint, Michigan, and got to play for the WNBA team close to her home. She was incredibly quick and able to get to the rim no matter what the defense did to try to stop her. One of her biggest shots was a corner 3-pointer with 53 seconds left that sealed the clinching game of the 2003 WNBA Finals. When the Shock moved to Tulsa after the 2009 season, Nolan didn't go with them and never returned to the WNBA. But she continued to play overseas for several years. -- Voepel

26. Alyssa Thomas
F | Connecticut Sun (2014-24); Phoenix Mercury (2025-present)

Career stats: 12.7 PPG, 7.7 RPG, 5.4 APG

Highlights: Three-time all-WNBA first team; seven-time All-Defensive team; two-time assists leader (2025, 2026); one-time rebounding leader (2023); one-time steals leader (2020)

Because she has the unfortunate timing of playing much of her career at the same time as A'ja Wilson and Breanna Stewart, Thomas does not have an MVP or a WNBA championship. But she has a statistical profile that is the most distinctive and versatile in league history. She's the only player with 5,000 points, 3,000 rebounds and 2,000 assists. No frontcourt player has more career assists, and Thomas is the all-time playoff leader in assists and double-doubles. She has 30 career triple-doubles. The next-highest player has five. -- Creme

27. Jonquel Jones
C | Connecticut Sun (2016-2022); New York Liberty (2023-present)

Career stats: 13.5 PPG, 8.5 RPG, 1.3 BPG

Highlights: One championship (2014); one Finals MVP (2014); MVP (2021); Most Improved (2017); Sixth Woman of the Year (2018); three-time rebounding leader; four-time All-Defensive team

From her dominant rebounding and shot-blocking talents to her ability to shoot 3-pointers, Jones is one of the most versatile centers in WNBA history. A steady career growth exploded with 2021's MVP award. Three years later, she helped lead the Liberty to their first WNBA title. Jones ranks 13th all time in blocked shots and rebounds, and is a career 38.5% 3-point shooter, a number that jumps to nearly 40% in four seasons in New York. -- Creme

28. Rebekkah Brunson
F | Sacramento Monarchs (2004-09); Minnesota Lynx (2010-18)

Career stats: 9.2 PPG, 7.4 RPG, 46.6 FG%

Highlights: Five championships (2005, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017); sixth all time in rebounds; seven-time All-Defensive team

With a nose for the ball and a willingness to do the little things, Brunson has more rings than any player in WNBA history. She would set screens, dive for loose balls and take on the toughest defensive assignment. That made her the perfect fit with Moore, Whalen and eventually Fowles for Minnesota's championship run of four titles in seven years. Much of Brunson's scoring came as a result of her hard work on the offensive glass; she remains second all time to Fowles in offensive rebounding. -- Creme

29. Swin Cash
F | Detroit Shock (2002-07); Seattle Storm (2008-11); Chicago Sky (2012-13); Atlanta Dream (2014), New York Liberty (2014-16)

Career stats: 10.7 PPG, 5.3 RPG, 2.4 APG

Highlights: Three championships (2003, 2006, 2010); two-time All-Star Game MVP

Cash was the No. 2 pick behind UConn teammate Sue Bird in 2002, and then won a championship the next year. She and the Shock won another title in 2006, and then Cash was traded to Seattle, where she rejoined Bird and won her third championship. Cash was never on the first team for All-WNBA or defense. Yet she is a player who could change games with her effort and energy, along with her talent. -- Voepel

30. Becky Hammon
G | New York Liberty (1999-2006); San Antonio Stars (2007-14)

Career stats: 13.0 PPG, 2.5 RPG, 3.8 APG

Highlights: 10th in career assists and fifth in 3-pointers; one-time assists leader; two-time All-WNBA first team

Hammon was famously undrafted in 1999, but with a caveat: That was the season many veteran players were in the draft after the ABL shut down. But that disappointment didn't stop Hammon, who made the Liberty roster that year and had a 16-season WNBA career. She played in the WNBA Finals three times with New York and once with San Antonio. At just 5-6, Hammon was known for her fearless ability to get to the rim despite her size, and she was one of the league's best 3-point shooters. Now as a coach of the Las Vegas Aces, Hammon has won three titles. -- Voepel

How the voting was done
As was the case for our 2021 ranking, we asked a panel to cast their vote for the greatest players in WNBA history "based on the players' overall performance on court, stats, championships, all-league honors and awards they won."

ESPN reporters, on-camera analysts and play-by-play broadcasters who cover the WNBA were invited to vote, as were staff from ESPN Research and the WNBA production, programming and PR teams at ESPN.

Twenty-three voters submitted ballots. The panel consisted of Rebecca Lobo, Carolyn Peck, Ryan Ruocco and Brooke Weisbrod; reporters Michael Voepel, Alexa Philippou, Kendra Andrews, Kareem Copeland, Charlie Creme, Katie Barnes, Sean Hurd, Andre Snellings and Shane Laflin; Jennifer LaCroix, Robbie Shamirian, Zack Collura, Jason Joseph and Jarod Hamilton of ESPN Research; Rodney Vaughn and Olivia Powers of ESPN Production; Shay Smith of ESPN Programming; Alex Feuz of ESPN PR; and editor Melanie Jackson.

stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Texas for the United States Grand Prix, with the championship battle set to heat up at the Circuit of the Americas.

Max Verstappen claimed his second victory this season after winning the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli continued to extend his lead in the title championship to 102 points from Mercedes teammate George Russell, and there is a mathematical chance he will be able to clinch the title in Austin.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 18th round.

- F1 still planning Middle East finale amid Kimi Antonelli title uncertainty - sources

- Franco Colapinto urges fans to stop 'attacking' Formula 1 drivers on social media

United States Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 23

Practice One: 6.30 p.m. - 7.30 p.m.

Practice Two: 10 p.m. - 11 p.m.

Saturday, October 24

Final Practice: 6.30 p.m. - 7.30 p.m.

Qualifying: 10 p.m. - 11 p.m.

Sunday, October 25

United States Grand Prix: 8 p.m. (GMT)

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the United States Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

It's a mix of fast corners, long straights and has one of the steepest elevation climbs to Turn 1.

Most poles: Hamilton (2007, 2016-2018) is tied with Michael Schumacher (2000-2002, 2006) on four. Other pole sitters from the current grid are Verstappen (2021 and 2025), Carlos Sainz (2022), Leclerc (2023) and Lando Norris (2024).

Weather forecast

The weather for the United States Grand Prix is expected to be light rain with a gentle breeze throughout the course of the weekend, with highs of 32°C.

What happened last time out?
Verstappen edged out Norris to take an imperious pole position by 0.291 seconds.

The Red Bull driver dominated the race and posed as a serious threat to McLaren's Norris and Oscar Piastri in the drivers' championship.

Norris finished second and cut his lead to 14 points to Piastri in the standings, who finished fifth. Verstappen ended the weekend only 40 points behind Piastri with five races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.
